questions.stem: A 61 year old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has 2 months of a tight, enormously swollen abdomen and has gained 9 kg. The abdomen is tense and the umbilicus is everted. The doctor places the patient's hand firmly on the midline and taps one flank while feeling the other.
questions.q: Which is the most likely finding?
o: A fluid thrill transmitted to the opposite flank
questions.e: Large-volume ascites gives a fluid thrill (the hand in the midline stops transmission through fat) and shifting dullness.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
**Tense** distension with weight gain in cirrhosis and the examiner is testing for a **thrill**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: A fluid thrill transmitted to the opposite flank.

elim: Ascites does not silence the bowel; that suggests ileus or peritonitis.
The opposite of ascites; suggests a central mass or distended bladder.
An abdominal aortic aneurysm.
Gastric outlet obstruction.

steps.x: **A. A fluid thrill transmitted to the opposite flank.** Ascites signs: shifting dullness and fluid thrill (large volume).

questions.stem: A 58 year old woman with hepatitis C has noticed her trousers no longer fit over 6 weeks. The swelling is painless. She is mildly breathless when lying flat. There are spider naevi, dilated veins on the abdominal wall and pitting oedema to both knees. The flanks are dull to percussion and the dullness moves when she rolls onto her side. Her temperature is 36.8°C.
questions.q: Which is the most likely cause of her abdominal swelling?
questions.e: Painless distension with shifting dullness, superficial veins, peripheral oedema and stigmata of chronic liver disease is ascites from portal hypertension.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.

clues: dilated veins on the abdominal wall
steps.x: **Painless** distension, **shifting dullness**, abdominal wall veins and chronic liver disease signs.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Ascites from portal hypertension.

elim: Gives colicky pain, vomiting and a tympanic abdomen.
Fat does not give shifting dullness or dilated abdominal veins.
A pelvic mass is dull centrally with resonant flanks.
A suprapubic dull mass, not shifting flank dullness.

steps.x: **A. Ascites from portal hypertension.** Shifting dullness + chronic liver disease signs = portal-hypertensive ascites.

questions.stem: A 66 year old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis and ascites has become more confused over 2 days and his urine output has fallen. He has no abdominal pain. His temperature is 37.6°C, pulse rate 98 bpm and BP 102/60 mmHg. His creatinine has risen from 88 to 156 µmol/L. A diagnostic tap shows cloudy fluid with 420 neutrophils/mm³.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: SBP can present with only encephalopathy or renal impairment. An ascitic neutrophil count above 250/mm³ confirms it.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
Confusion and AKI with ascites; the tap has **over 250 neutrophils**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

elim: Gives tremor and agitation, not raised ascitic neutrophils.
Renal failure is present, but neutrophils over 250 mean infection must be treated.
Loin pain and dysuria with pyuria; the ascitic fluid is the infected site.
Needs a perforation or abscess with a rigid abdomen and multiple organisms.

steps.x: **E. Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.** Any deterioration with ascites: tap it; >250 neutrophils = SBP.

questions.stem: A 59 year old woman who has never drunk alcohol has type 2 diabetes and a BMI of 39. She has 2 months of abdominal swelling. There is shifting dullness and splenomegaly. Ultrasound shows a small nodular liver and ascites. The serum-ascites albumin gradient is 1.5 g/dL. Viral and autoimmune screens are negative.
questions.q: Which is the most likely underlying cause of her ascites?
o: Cirrhosis from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
questions.e: Cirrhosis is the most important cause of ascites; here a nodular liver, high gradient and metabolic risk factors point to NAFLD cirrhosis.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
**High gradient** with a **nodular liver** and metabolic risk factors, no alcohol.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Cirrhosis from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

elim: Low gradient ascites with heavy proteinuria and a normal liver.
Peritoneal disease gives a low gradient and a pelvic mass.
Low gradient, lymphocytic fluid, fever and weight loss.
High gradient but with a raised JVP and a smooth congested liver.

steps.x: **A. Cirrhosis from non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.** Most ascites is cirrhotic; check the SAAG and the liver.

questions.stem: A 64 year old woman with cirrhosis and ascites has 1 day of a more swollen, diffusely sore abdomen. She feels shivery. Her temperature is 37.9°C, pulse rate 104 bpm and BP 110/68 mmHg. The abdomen is distended and tender all over but soft, with no guarding. Bowel sounds are present. An erect chest X-ray shows no free air.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Ascites with fever, abdominal pain, distension and tenderness, without free air, is SBP until a tap shows otherwise.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
Triad of **ascites, fever and abdominal pain** with diffuse tenderness and no perforation.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

elim: Pain localises to the right iliac fossa with guarding.
Colicky RUQ pain without fever or distension.
Free air under the diaphragm and board-like rigidity.
Gives distension but not fever with diffuse tenderness.

steps.x: **D. Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.** Ascites + fever + abdominal pain = SBP, a medical emergency.

questions.stem: A 55 year old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has developed ascites. He has spider naevi and palmar erythema. He feels well otherwise. His temperature is 36.8°C and BP 112/70 mmHg. His platelet count is 82 ×10⁹/L with a normal white cell count. The doctor examines his left upper quadrant.
questions.q: Which is the most likely additional finding?
questions.e: Ascites comes with other signs of portal hypertension: splenomegaly (with a low platelet count), caput medusae and varices.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
Ascites plus a **low platelet count**: look for another sign of **portal hypertension**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Splenomegaly.

elim: A palpable gallbladder with painless jaundice from pancreatic cancer.
Suggests colonic or diverticular disease.
An abdominal aortic aneurysm.
Renal artery stenosis.

steps.x: **E. Splenomegaly.** Portal hypertension: ascites, splenomegaly, caput medusae, varices.

questions.stem: A 60 year old man with cirrhosis and ascites had spontaneous bacterial peritonitis 4 months ago and was started on prophylactic antibiotics. He stopped taking them last month. He now has 2 days of abdominal pain and fever. His temperature is 38.4°C and pulse rate 108 bpm. His abdomen is distended and tender without guarding.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Ascites can become infected; previous SBP and stopping prophylaxis make recurrence likely. Fever and abdominal pain with ascites is SBP.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
Previous **SBP**, prophylaxis **stopped**, now fever and pain.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Recurrent spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.

elim: Localised RUQ pain with Murphy's sign.
Epigastric pain to the back with high amylase.
Left iliac fossa pain in an older patient.
Sudden pain with haemoperitoneum and shock.

steps.x: **E. Recurrent spontaneous bacterial peritonitis.** Infected ascites recurs; prophylaxis protects.

questions.stem: A 57 year old woman with cirrhosis had 9 litres of tense ascites drained in a day unit. No albumin was given. Two days later she is dizzy and passing little urine. Her pulse rate is 112 bpm and BP 86/52 mmHg. Her creatinine has risen from 82 to 190 µmol/L and sodium has fallen to 126 mmol/L. The ascites has started to re-accumulate.
questions.q: Which is the most likely cause of her deterioration?
questions.e: Large-volume paracentesis without albumin cover worsens splanchnic vasodilation and effective circulating volume, causing paracentesis-induced circulatory dysfunction with hypotension, AKI and hyponatraemia.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
Large drain **without albumin**, then **hypotension, AKI, hyponatraemia**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Paracentesis-induced circulatory dysfunction.

elim: Not caused by abdominal paracentesis and gives no hyponatraemia.
Would give peritonitis with fever and guarding.
Would cause a falling Hb and visible bleeding.
Fever and tenderness would be expected, and it does not follow from drainage itself.

steps.x: **D. Paracentesis-induced circulatory dysfunction.** LVP needs IV human albumin solution to prevent circulatory dysfunction.

questions.stem: A 63 year old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has fever and a tender, distended abdomen. His temperature is 38.2°C and pulse rate 106 bpm. A diagnostic ascitic tap is sent for cell count and albumin within 2 hours.
questions.q: Which ascitic fluid result would confirm the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: SBP is diagnosed when ascitic neutrophils exceed 250 cells/mm³.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.

clues: fever and a tender, distended abdomen
steps.x: Fever with tender ascites: the **neutrophil** count decides.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Neutrophils 380 cells/mm³.

elim: A high ascitic albumin points to a low SAAG cause, not infection.
A lymphocytic fluid suggests TB or malignancy.
Below 250 does not confirm SBP.
Blood-stained fluid suggests a traumatic tap or malignancy.

steps.x: **D. Neutrophils 380 cells/mm³.** SBP = ascitic neutrophils >250 cells/mm³.

questions.stem: A 52 year old man has 3 months of painless abdominal swelling. He drinks heavily. There is shifting dullness and the veins around his umbilicus are dilated, with blood flowing away from the umbilicus. He has a palpable spleen. His temperature is 36.9°C and BP 114/70 mmHg.
questions.q: Which is the most likely cause of the dilated veins?
questions.e: Veins radiating from the umbilicus (caput medusae) with splenomegaly and ascites are signs of portal hypertension.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
**Caput medusae**, splenomegaly and ascites together.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Portal hypertension.

elim: Veins fill from below upwards on the flanks, not radiating from the umbilicus.
Raises the JVP and congests the liver but does not cause caput medusae.
Infection of ascites, not a cause of collateral veins.
Gives facial swelling and chest wall veins flowing downwards.

steps.x: **B. Portal hypertension.** Ascites + caput medusae + splenomegaly = portal hypertension.

questions.stem: A 49 year old woman with chronic hepatitis B attends clinic. She has gained 5 kg in 4 weeks despite a poor appetite and feels full after small meals. Her abdomen is distended with flank dullness. Ultrasound shows an irregular, shrunken liver and free fluid. The serum-ascites albumin gradient is 1.8 g/dL.
questions.q: Which is the most likely cause of her weight gain?
questions.e: Weight gain with distension in chronic liver disease is ascites; a high gradient and shrunken irregular liver mean cirrhosis, the most important cause.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.
Weight up, appetite down, **free fluid**, cirrhotic liver, **high SAAG**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Ascites from cirrhosis.

elim: Weight gain without flank dullness or free fluid.
Low gradient and heavy proteinuria.
Low gradient ascites with a pelvic mass.
Ultrasound would show a gravid uterus; the liver is cirrhotic.

steps.x: **A. Ascites from cirrhosis.** Weight gain + distension in liver disease = ascites; cirrhosis is the commonest cause.

questions.stem: A 62 year old man has new ascites. He drinks 50 units of alcohol a week. Ultrasound shows a coarse nodular liver, splenomegaly and reversed flow in the portal vein. An ascitic tap shows 30 neutrophils/mm³ and an albumin of 9 g/L, with serum albumin 27 g/L.
questions.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of his ascites?
questions.e: The SAAG is 27 minus 9 = 18 g/L (1.8 g/dL), at least 1.1, so this is a portal-hypertensive transudate; the commonest cause is cirrhosis.

steps.x: It asks for a diagnosis-type answer: build the picture from the history, observations and tests.

clues: reversed flow in the portal vein
steps.x: SAAG = 27 − 9 = **18 g/L (1.8 g/dL)** with a cirrhotic liver.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Portal hypertension due to cirrhosis.

elim: Neutrophils are 30/mm³, far below 250.
Chylous ascites with a low gradient.
Low gradient and lymphocytic fluid.
Nephrotic ascites has a low gradient.

steps.x: **D. Portal hypertension due to cirrhosis.** Most ascites = portal hypertension from cirrhosis; SAAG ≥1.1 confirms the portal cause.

questions.stem: A 55 year old man with a BMI of 42 and alcohol-related liver disease feels his abdomen is getting bigger. Examination is difficult because of his body habitus and the doctor cannot be sure whether there is shifting dullness. He is otherwise well. His temperature is 36.7°C.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation for ascites?
questions.e: Ultrasound of the abdomen is both the initial investigation and the gold standard for detecting ascites, especially when examination is unreliable.

steps.x: It asks about a test: decide what question the test must answer at this point.

clues: cannot be sure whether there is shifting dullness
steps.x: Examination **unreliable** because of habitus: image for fluid.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Ultrasound abdomen.

elim: Insensitive for fluid; shows a ground-glass appearance only with large volumes.
Detects fluid but uses radiation and contrast; ultrasound is first and gold standard.
A blind tap risks bowel injury when ascites is not confirmed.
Not needed to detect ascites.

steps.x: **E. Ultrasound abdomen.** Ascites: ultrasound abdomen is initial and gold standard.

questions.stem: A 59 year old woman with cirrhosis and ascites is admitted at 10:00 with fever and abdominal tenderness. Her temperature is 38.3°C and pulse rate 102 bpm. Her INR is 1.7 and platelets 74 ×10⁹/L. The ward is busy and the junior doctor plans to do the ascitic tap tomorrow morning.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate timing for the diagnostic ascitic tap?
o: After correcting the INR to below 1.2
Only if blood cultures are positive
Tomorrow morning on the ward round
questions.e: Suspected SBP needs a diagnostic paracentesis within 8 hours; a raised INR and low platelets do not contraindicate a diagnostic tap.

steps.x: It asks about a test: decide what question the test must answer at this point.
Suspected **SBP**: an emergency with a time target.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Within 8 hours of suspected SBP.

elim: Antibiotics first sterilise the fluid and reduce diagnostic yield.
Coagulopathy is not a reason to delay a diagnostic tap.
Most SBP has negative blood cultures; the tap is the key test.
Delaying the tap delays diagnosis and treatment of a medical emergency.

steps.x: **E. Within 8 hours of suspected SBP.** Tap within 8 hours of suspected SBP.

questions.stem: A 61 year old man with known cirrhosis is admitted with worsening ascites. He is alert. His temperature is 36.9°C, pulse rate 84 bpm and BP 112/70 mmHg. A diagnostic tap is planned and diuretics are being considered. The F1 asks which blood tests should be sent first.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate set of blood tests?
questions.e: First-line bloods in ascites are LFTs, U&Es and INR to assess liver function and renal function before diuretics.

steps.x: It asks about a test: decide what question the test must answer at this point.
**Diuretics planned**: need kidneys and liver function.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: LFTs, U&Es and INR.

elim: Pancreatic tests; no epigastric pain.
Not first-line; raised in any ascites.
Not relevant to ascites assessment.
Cardiac markers, not first-line here.

steps.x: **C. LFTs, U&Es and INR.** Ascites bloods: LFTs, U&Es, INR, then ascitic tap.

questions.stem: A 48 year old woman has new ascites and a raised JVP. Her liver is enlarged and tender. Echocardiogram shows a thickened, calcified pericardium. Serum albumin is 34 g/L and ascitic albumin 15 g/L. Ascitic neutrophils are 40/mm³.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate interpretation of the ascitic fluid result?
questions.e: SAAG = 34 − 15 = 19 g/L (1.9 g/dL), at least 1.1, so portal-hypertensive. Constrictive pericarditis is one such cause alongside cirrhosis, Budd-Chiari and right heart failure.

steps.x: It asks about a test: decide what question the test must answer at this point.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: High gradient, portal-hypertensive transudate.

elim: Neutrophils are 40/mm³, so not infected; a high gradient is a transudate.
The gradient is 1.9 g/dL, above 1.1.
Nephrotic ascites has a low gradient.
TB gives a low gradient with lymphocytes.

steps.x: **B. High gradient, portal-hypertensive transudate.** SAAG ≥1.1 g/dL = portal hypertension (cirrhosis, constrictive pericarditis, Budd-Chiari, right HF).

questions.stem: A 34 year old man from Somalia has 2 months of fever, night sweats, weight loss and abdominal swelling. There is shifting dullness and a doughy abdomen. His liver is normal on ultrasound. A diagnostic ascitic tap shows a lymphocyte-rich fluid. His serum albumin is 30 g/L.
questions.q: Which is the most likely serum-ascites albumin gradient?
o: Exactly zero, because the gradient is not valid in infection
It cannot be calculated without an ascitic protein
questions.e: Peritoneal TB is an exudative, non-portal-hypertensive process, so the SAAG is below 1.1 g/dL, as with peritoneal carcinomatosis.

steps.x: It asks about a test: decide what question the test must answer at this point.
**Normal liver**, systemic features, **lymphocytic** fluid.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Less than 1.1 g/dL.

elim: A high gradient means portal hypertension; his liver is normal.
The gradient is valid in infection and is low here.
A very high gradient would mean severe portal hypertension.
SAAG needs only serum and ascitic albumin.

steps.x: **E. Less than 1.1 g/dL.** SAAG <1.1 g/dL = non-portal cause (carcinomatosis, TB).

questions.stem: A 58 year old man with cirrhosis and ascites has mild abdominal discomfort but no fever. His temperature is 37.1°C, pulse rate 82 bpm and BP 118/74 mmHg. His abdomen is soft and non-tender. A diagnostic tap shows clear fluid with 180 neutrophils/mm³.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate interpretation of this result?
questions.e: SBP is diagnosed when ascitic neutrophils exceed 250 cells/mm³; 180 does not confirm it.

steps.x: It asks about a test: decide what question the test must answer at this point.
Neutrophils **below 250** and a well patient.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: SBP is not confirmed.

elim: Culture-negative SBP still needs neutrophils above 250.
The threshold is above 250 cells/mm³.
Requires a surgical source with a very high neutrophil count.
TB gives a lymphocytic fluid.

steps.x: **C. SBP is not confirmed.** SBP threshold: >250 neutrophils/mm³.

questions.stem: A 56 year old woman with cirrhosis is admitted with new, moderate ascites. She has no fever or pain. Her temperature is 36.8°C. A diagnostic tap is performed and the registrar asks which two tests on the ascitic fluid matter most at this stage.
questions.q: Which are the most appropriate ascitic fluid tests?
questions.e: The key ascitic tests are the cell count (neutrophils, for SBP) and albumin (for the SAAG, for the cause).

steps.x: It asks about a test: decide what question the test must answer at this point.
One test for **infection**, one for **cause**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Cell count and albumin.

elim: Only for suspected pancreatic or chylous ascites.
Help distinguish secondary peritonitis but are not the key first tests.
Insensitive; the neutrophil count diagnoses SBP.
Not standard first-line ascitic tests.

steps.x: **B. Cell count and albumin.** Ascitic tap: neutrophil count (SBP) + albumin (SAAG).

questions.stem: A 54 year old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has his first episode of ascites. He has stopped drinking. He has no fever or pain and his abdomen is soft. His temperature is 36.9°C. Ultrasound has confirmed moderate free fluid.
questions.q: Which is the next most appropriate investigation?
o: Diagnostic paracentesis with ascitic fluid analysis
questions.e: All new ascites needs a diagnostic tap for cell count (to exclude SBP) and albumin (to calculate SAAG), even without symptoms.

steps.x: It asks about a test: decide what question the test must answer at this point.
Fluid **confirmed**: now characterise it.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Diagnostic paracentesis with ascitic fluid analysis.

elim: Ultrasound has already shown the fluid; CT adds little.
Reserved for unexplained low gradient ascites.
Not needed to investigate ascites.
Screens for varices but does not characterise ascites.

steps.x: **B. Diagnostic paracentesis with ascitic fluid analysis.** New ascites: diagnostic paracentesis (cell count, albumin).

questions.stem: A 60 year old woman with cirrhosis has moderate ascites. She has lost muscle bulk and eats ready meals and crisps most days. Her BMI is 19. Her sodium is 134 mmol/L and creatinine 72 µmol/L. She has been started on a diuretic and asks what she should eat.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate dietary advice?
o: Fluid restriction to 500 mL a day
High-salt diet to protect her sodium
Salt restriction with a high-energy, high-protein diet
questions.e: Ascites is managed with dietary salt restriction and a high-energy, high-protein diet, alongside diuretics.

steps.x: It asks for a management step: decide how unwell the patient is and what comes first.
**Salty** food and **malnourished**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Salt restriction with a high-energy, high-protein diet.

elim: Not needed with sodium of 134; salt drives fluid retention.
Salt worsens ascites.
Worsens malnutrition.
She is already underweight.

steps.x: **D. Salt restriction with a high-energy, high-protein diet.** Ascites diet: low salt, high energy, high protein.

questions.stem: A 57 year old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis and ascites has taken spironolactone 100 mg once daily with salt restriction for 1 week. He has lost only 0.5 kg. His sodium is 136 mmol/L, potassium 4.3 mmol/L and creatinine 80 µmol/L. His BP is 118/72 mmHg.

o: Increase spironolactone, titrating towards 400 mg daily
questions.e: First-line is spironolactone 100 mg OD, titrated up to 400 mg OD with furosemide added, while electrolytes and renal function allow.

steps.x: It asks for a management step: decide how unwell the patient is and what comes first.
Starting dose, poor response, **normal potassium and creatinine**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Increase spironolactone, titrating towards 400 mg daily.

elim: For tense or refractory ascites, not inadequate response to a starting dose.
Thiazides are not used for ascites.
He is tolerating it with normal electrolytes.
For refractory ascites after maximal diuretics.

steps.x: **A. Increase spironolactone, titrating towards 400 mg daily.** Spironolactone 100 mg → titrate to 400 mg (± furosemide).

questions.stem: A 53 year old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has moderate ascites controlled on spironolactone and furosemide with salt restriction. He still drinks 40 units a week. His temperature is 36.8°C. He asks what else will most help his ascites in the long term.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate long-term measure?
o: Reduce drinking to 14 units a week
questions.e: Treat the underlying cause where possible: stopping alcohol in alcohol-related cirrhosis can improve liver function and ascites.

steps.x: It asks for a management step: decide how unwell the patient is and what comes first.
Ongoing **alcohol** is the treatable cause.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Complete abstinence from alcohol.

elim: Not needed for controlled ascites.
Not needed without hyponatraemia.
Any alcohol keeps injuring the cirrhotic liver.
They are controlling his ascites.

steps.x: **A. Complete abstinence from alcohol.** Treat the cause: stop alcohol.

questions.stem: A 62 year old woman with cirrhosis has tense ascites causing breathlessness. She also has bleeding gums and oozing from cannula sites. Her platelets are 38 ×10⁹/L, fibrinogen 0.8 g/L (1.5–4.0) and D-dimer markedly raised. Large-volume paracentesis had been planned for this morning.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
o: Postpone paracentesis and treat the coagulopathy
questions.e: Large-volume paracentesis is contraindicated in DIC (bleeding gums, raised D-dimer, low fibrinogen); the coagulopathy is managed first.

Tense ascites **but DIC**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Postpone paracentesis and treat the coagulopathy.

Contraindicated, and albumin cover would be needed anyway.

steps.x: **C. Postpone paracentesis and treat the coagulopathy.** No large-volume paracentesis in DIC.

questions.stem: A 70 kg man with cirrhosis has spontaneous bacterial peritonitis confirmed by an ascitic neutrophil count of 610/mm³. He has started IV ceftriaxone. His creatinine is 132 µmol/L and bilirubin 70 µmol/L. The pharmacist asks for the human albumin solution prescription.

o: 1.5 g/kg within 6 hours, then 1 g/kg on day 3
8 g per litre of fluid drained
No albumin unless BP falls below 90 mmHg

steps.x: It asks for a management step: decide how unwell the patient is and what comes first.
SBP confirmed and on antibiotics: now the **albumin** dose.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: 1.5 g/kg within 6 hours, then 1 g/kg on day 3.

elim: Too little to protect renal function.
Not the recommended regimen.
The regimen for large-volume paracentesis, not SBP.
Albumin is given in SBP to prevent renal failure.

steps.x: **C. 1.5 g/kg within 6 hours, then 1 g/kg on day 3.** SBP albumin: 1.5 g/kg in 6 h, 1 g/kg on day 3.

questions.stem: A 65 year old woman with cirrhosis and ascites has fever and abdominal pain. Her temperature is 38.6°C, pulse rate 110 bpm and BP 100/62 mmHg. A diagnostic tap shows 520 neutrophils/mm³. Ascitic fluid culture results will take 48 hours.
questions.q: Which is the next most appropriate step in management?
o: Large-volume paracentesis to remove infected fluid
Repeat the tap in 48 hours before treating
Wait for culture results before starting antibiotics
questions.e: Ascitic neutrophils above 250 confirm SBP; IV antibiotics such as ceftriaxone start immediately without waiting for culture.

steps.x: It asks for a management step: decide how unwell the patient is and what comes first.
Diagnosis **already confirmed** by the count.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Start intravenous ceftriaxone now.

elim: Drainage does not treat SBP and risks circulatory collapse.
Prophylaxis is for prevention; active SBP needs IV treatment.
Delay increases mortality.
Neutrophils over 250 are enough to treat.

steps.x: **D. Start intravenous ceftriaxone now.** SBP: treat on the neutrophil count with IV ceftriaxone (plus albumin).

questions.stem: A 58 year old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has been abstinent for a year. Despite salt restriction and maximum tolerated diuretics, he has needed large-volume paracentesis five times in 8 weeks. He has no history of encephalopathy. His bilirubin is 30 µmol/L and echocardiogram is normal.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate referral?
questions.e: Recurrent or refractory ascites despite salt restriction and maximal diuretics should be referred for TIPS, if there is no encephalopathy or heart failure.

steps.x: It asks for a management step: decide how unwell the patient is and what comes first.
**Refractory**, recurrent ascites, no encephalopathy, normal heart.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt.

elim: Above the maximum dose and he is already at maximum tolerated diuretics.
Rarely used, with high complication rates.
Does not treat ascites.
Largely replaced by TIPS.

steps.x: **E. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt.** Refractory ascites: refer for TIPS.

questions.stem: A 59 year old man with cirrhosis has ascites and ankle oedema. His serum albumin is 24 g/L and ultrasound shows a nodular liver with an enlarged portal vein. A student asks why fluid collects in his peritoneal cavity.
questions.q: Which is the most likely mechanism?
o: Increased capillary permeability from peritoneal inflammation
Raised central venous pressure from left heart failure
Raised sinusoidal hydrostatic pressure and low plasma oncotic pressure

questions.stem: A 56 year old woman with cirrhosis and ascites has a low BP of 98/58 mmHg and very low urinary sodium. Her plasma renin and aldosterone are high, although her total body sodium and water are increased. A student asks why her kidneys behave as if she were dehydrated.
